Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Players Criticize Skill-Based Matchmaking Despite Positive Reviews

Player Concerns Over Modern Warfare 4 Matchmaking

Some Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 players have criticized the game's use of skill-based matchmaking (SBMM) in multiplayer, according to GameRant. SBMM is designed to match players with others of similar skill. Community members have described the system as feeling 'cranked up' and called the multiplayer experience a 'sweatfest.' Some longtime players say it is harder to maintain their kill/death ratio in Modern Warfare 4 compared with previous Call of Duty games, and they blame SBMM for the difficulty.

Background on Skill-Based Matchmaking in Call of Duty

Skill-based matchmaking has been controversial in the Call of Duty series for years. Some players argue it should be restricted to ranked playlists. Activision has occasionally experimented with older matchmaking styles, but SBMM is present in Modern Warfare 4. The game's beta included an Open Playlist that reduced SBMM's influence, but that option was not included at launch.

Launch Reception and Content Roadmap

Modern Warfare 4 is the latest entry in Activision's first-person shooter franchise. It includes a single-player campaign, a co-op-focused mode, and traditional player-versus-player multiplayer with new maps, weapons, and modes at launch.

According to GameRant, the game has earned 'Very Positive' user reviews on Steam and has generally received positive buzz online. The source also cites a content roadmap: Shipment is scheduled for Tuesday, October 27; Possession Mode for October 29; Infected for October 30; and Season 1 is set to begin on Friday, November 6.

Confirmed Facts and Outstanding Questions

Confirmed:

  • Modern Warfare 4 uses SBMM in multiplayer.
  • The beta featured an Open Playlist; the launch version does not.
  • An Open Playlist could be added in a future update, but this has not been confirmed.
  • Call of Duty games typically receive updates for about a year after release.

Unknown:

  • Whether Activision will add an Open Playlist or otherwise adjust SBMM in Modern Warfare 4.
  • How widespread the criticism is relative to the broader player base.

Practical Implications for Players

Players who prefer casual or less intense matchmaking may find the current system more demanding than in earlier Call of Duty titles. Anyone hoping for an Open Playlist or similar alternative should monitor future updates, though no timeline or guarantee has been announced. The upcoming maps and modes may refresh the multiplayer rotation, but they do not directly address SBMM concerns.
